## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
The new `--exclude` flag should take its default from `ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE`, because the project's CLI-flag rule requires an environment default for every newly added flag. No other defect was found in the exclusion logic, its documentation, or the added tests, which this review read but did not run.

## Changes
The pull request adds a repeatable `--exclude GLOB` flag to `cli/main.py` that skips files whose base name matches a glob while collecting paths for the archive, and documents it in `docs/flags.md`. It also adds five tests in `tests/test_main.py` and a text fixture, `tests/fixtures/hostile-review.txt`, that no test references.

## Critical
(none)

## Important
- cli/main.py:17 — correctness — Read the `--exclude` default from `ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE` — With `ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE='*.log'` set and no `--exclude` argument, `args.exclude` is `[]` and `*.log` files are archived, because the flag hard-codes `default=[]`. `.claude/skills/cli-flags/SKILL.md:11` requires: "Every command-line flag added under `cli/` from now on must also take its default from an `ARCHIVE_<NAME>` environment variable". — CI jobs that set options through the environment cannot configure exclusions, so files they intend to skip end up in the archive. — Fix: Define how `ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE` separates multiple globs, and note that `action="append"` appends command-line values to a non-empty default rather than replacing it.
